text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000013 bills 99215 well above its risk-adjusted expectation, with elevated rates even among patients with few chronic conditions, but no 99215 charts came back to confirm or refute the coding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The complexity breakdown shows a pattern consistent with upcoding: this provider's 99215 share runs roughly double the all-provider rate in the 0-, 1- and 2-condition strata, and nearly half of its 99215s fall on low-complexity patients. Sampled examples include visits coded only for nonspecific complaints such as R10.9, N39.0, M54.50 or Z09 (e.g., C0005114, C0005641, C0005656, C0005529). Against that, the high-complexity sampled 99215s (e.g., C0005928, C0006316) look clinically plausible, the plain peer z-score is unremarkable, and the 4-condition stratum actually bills below peers. The documentation cannot settle it: only 18 charts returned, none for a 99215, and the single unsupported 99214 (C0006003) is too little to draw on, while the data-reviewed notes all had matching lab or test lines. A reviewer should first request charts for the sampled low-complexity 99215 claims, starting with the symptom-only and follow-up (Z09) visits, to see whether documented MDM or time supports the high level."}
